requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Every volume axis starts at 0. Share graphics express magnitude on a percentage scale, including labelled parts of a whole where no axis is appropriate. Chart form may vary; truncated volume axes or shares plotted as annual volumes fail.

Require a two-page specification covering source columns, selected chart types, annual and monthly units, sector colours and markers, publication surfaces, required wording and a data check note. It records Residential #0072B2/circle, Industrial #E69F00/square, Public #009E73/triangle and Ecological #CC79A7/diamond; million m³/year; million m³/month; and Source: CLEARWATER, 2026. The note locates the 2026 CSV row and named sector columns, verifies Total 315.1 and Residential 160.8, and describes the share calculation using denominator 315.1. Where delivery chronology is available, it precedes the designs; do not infer chronology from page order alone. Missing specification subjects or incorrect source references fail.

The overview shows 2026 Residential 160.8, Industrial 78.6, Public 42.5, Ecological 33.2 and Total 315.1. For years 2022–2026 respectively, the trends label Residential [148.2,151.6,154.9,157.3,160.8], Industrial [96.5,92.1,87.4,83.0,78.6], Public [41.3,42.0,41.7,43.1,42.5], Ecological [18.0,21.4,25.8,29.6,33.2] and Total [304.0,307.1,309.8,313.0,315.1]. The card includes that complete Total series and 2026 Residential 160.8. The share diagram associates the four sectors in that order with 51.0%,24.9%,13.5%,10.5%, explains the 99.9% rounded sum and states sector value ÷ 315.1 × 100. The hot-season chart identifies Residential, 2026, May→14.8, June→15.7, July→17.1, August→16.3, Planning estimate and million m³/month. Chart forms may vary; omissions, substitutions or mismatched labels fail.

The summary combines the 2026 overview, all five annual Total points and the 2026 hot-season chart. The board combines the 2026 overview, 2026 shares and the 2026 hot-season chart. Overviews show Residential 160.8, Industrial 78.6, Public 42.5, Ecological 33.2 and Total 315.1 in million m³/year. The summary's Total series pairs 2022–2026 with 304.0,307.1,309.8,313.0,315.1. The board's shares are 51.0%,24.9%,13.5%,10.5% in sector order, with the denominator 315.1 calculation and 99.9% rounding explanation. Both monthly charts pair May–August with 14.8,15.7,17.1,16.3, identify 2026 Residential, and explicitly print Planning estimate and million m³/month. Rearrangement is allowed; missing chart components or incorrect records fail.

Each chart follows the specification's fixed sector mapping, direct names and correct annual, monthly or percentage unit. Require a title, Source: CLEARWATER, 2026 and a short accurate interpretation for each chart. Volume and share values have one decimal place; sector symbols and names remain identifiable without colour. Size and arrangement may adapt to the surface, but omitted metadata, changed encodings or unsupported annotations fail.

Inspect every embedded chart, including presentation reproductions. Each preserves the specification's sector colours, shapes and direct names; uses the correct annual, monthly or percentage unit; and includes a title, Source: CLEARWATER, 2026 and a supported reading annotation. Display volume and share values to one decimal place, start volume axes at zero, and keep shares on a percentage scale. Monthly values remain explicitly labelled Planning estimate. Symbols and names must survive grayscale reading. Resizing is allowed when these details remain legible; cropping away required chart information fails.

Both documents visibly repeat the specification's 2026 Total 315.1 and Residential 160.8 with million m³/year. The summary occupies one 210 × 297 mm portrait page and the board one 420 × 297 mm landscape page, each with at least 15 mm clear space on every edge. Content placement may vary; incorrect records, orientation or content intruding into those margins fails.

The card is portrait and visibly associates 2026 with Total 315.1 and Residential 160.8 in million m³/year, matching the specification. Flexible composition is allowed; missing year, unit or either figure fails.

Every image retains the supplied authority mark in #1B6CA8 and prints CLEARWATER. The overview and social card additionally print Water through the hot season. Scale and placement may vary; a replacement mark or missing required wording fails.

Each finished document visibly retains the authority mark in #1B6CA8 and prints CLEARWATER. The summary and board also print Water through the hot season. The presentation need not repeat standalone publication wording on every page, but reused surfaces must preserve their required wording. Missing document identity or publication wording fails.

Review the complete video and its duration. It lasts 12 seconds, uses the annual Total trend with 2022–2026 values 304.0,307.1,309.8,313.0,315.1, and finishes on a readable 2026 Total 315.1, million m³/year and Source: CLEARWATER, 2026. It retains the authority mark and CLEARWATER. Chart appearances preserve the specification's applicable encodings, titles, units, source credit and accurate reading annotations; volumes use one decimal place and zero-based axes. Animation style may vary. Incorrect duration, absent trend, inconsistent chart content or an incomplete closing frame fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: The presentation has at least eight pages and explicitly communicates all four sector colour-marker mappings, 2026 Total 315.1, Residential 160.8, million m³/year and Source: CLEARWATER, 2026 consistently with the specification. Facts may appear in readable reproduced pages or dedicated explanatory text. An incomplete mapping, altered fact or insufficient page count fails.

Locate recognisable, readable reuse of the specification, every supplied chart, the summary, social card, exhibition board and frames from the video. Scaling, excerpts and page rearrangement are acceptable when the source remains identifiable. A category mentioned only in text, unrelated replacements or omission of a listed source fails.
